precepts.text: All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, Hosea. He multiplied visions and used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.
precepts.point: In order to deal with these reoccurring events, we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors from the past, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

precepts.why:
The things written aforetime were written for our learning, and Hosea shows how they were written: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, even Hosea. God multiplied visions, and he used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.

That is how the scriptures teach us today. The past is a similitude of what is happening now, and by comparing one thing to another we can see our own time in what was written. The last beast of Revelation 13 is described with the leopard, the bear and the lion of Daniel 7: it carries the attributes of Greece, Persia and Media, and Babylon. The golden image of Daniel 3 stands again in our day.

So we read the prophets as similitudes, and through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, because the Most High already showed in the past what he will do in the future.

precepts.text: I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.
precepts.point: Video played on Agenda 21: a master plan to change the political and economic system of the world to total collectivism. People must be dependent on the state for everything; they cannot have private property or land of their own; they are to live in high-rise apartments provided as a benefit, because anybody with a couple of acres, his own water supply, and his own food is a threat to a collectivist society. You see BlackRock and Blackstone buying up housing across America, trying to get rid of private homes. It correlates to what happened in Egypt in Genesis 47: give us food, take care of us, and we give up our property and become servants. You don't think that will happen again? The things written aforetime were written for our learning.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” God speaks in similitudes. What happened in Egypt under Joseph is not just a nice story; it is a likeness of what is coming.

The Egyptians, when money failed, gave up their cattle, then their bodies and their lands, and became servants unto Pharaoh. That is a similitude of a people today, in the spiritual Egypt, who will give up their property and their freedom to the government in exchange for bread. The plans are being made behind the scenes now.

The same is true of the scriptures that follow: when the prophets speak of Egypt, understand the similitude. The Egypt of Isaiah 19 is Babylon the Great, the great city “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.”

precepts.text: He took his brother by the heel in the womb and by his strength he had power with God, yea, he had power over the angel and prevailed; his name was changed because of his strength.
precepts.point: Jacob was trained by Isaac and Abraham; imagine his descendants, David running through warriors, Samson; our forefathers were intellectual and physically powerful, and Jacob was a god on the earth.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.” He fought for hours. In a real fight you are exhausted long before daybreak; a boxing match is twelve rounds, and Jacob fought until the break of day. “when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh;” and put it out of joint. The angel had to dislocate Jacob’s thigh to stop him. Even then Jacob held on: “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me.”

“Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.” That is what the name means: a prince with power with God.

Hosea 12:3-4 says why his name was changed: “He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with God: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Beth–el, and there he spake with us.” By his strength. His name was changed to Israel because of how strong he was. This was no slap boxing; it went back and forth, and there is no other record in the Bible of any man wrestling with an angel and prevailing. Jacob was a god on the earth.

He was trained to fight. Abraham had trained servants, armed them, and went to war to bring Lot back; Isaac knew it as well, and they taught Jacob. Imagine his descendants: David running through warriors, Samson, a warlike race. Our forefathers were intellectual as well as physically powerful; Abraham knew arithmetic and taught astronomy. That is why this superiority is stressed: white people, and even some of our own who move in their circles, say we are stupid and have low IQ, and many of us believe it. The white teacher told Malcolm X, top of his class, that being a lawyer was no profession for a nigga, and he should be a carpenter. The scriptures say otherwise about the children of Israel.

precepts.text: I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets. A similitude shows you one thing, but it is really something else he is trying to explain. That is what Peter was pondering.
precepts.point: The vision was not really talking about food. That is why it says Peter doubted in himself what this vision should mean: is the Lord telling me to eat unlawful animals? When visions come from God, they are an allegory, referring to something else.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Peter fell into a trance and saw a vessel full of “fourfooted beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and fowls of the air”, and a voice said, “Rise, Peter; kill, and eat.” Peter answered, “Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean.” But the vision was not really talking about food. That is why it says “Peter doubted in himself what this vision which he had seen should mean”.

When visions come from God, they are an allegory, referring to something else many times. The Lord proves it himself: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude shows you one thing, but it is really something else he is trying to explain.

That is what Peter was pondering. Is the Lord telling me to eat unlawful animals? No, Lord, I have never eaten anything unlawful. The beasts in the sheet were a similitude, and Peter did not yet know what they stood for.

He found out when he came to Cornelius. He said, “God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.” The vision was not about unclean animals; it was about man. Cornelius was a just man and a devout man, and the vision was showing Peter that God is no respecter of persons, northern kingdom or southern kingdom: “in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” Israel, the ones called not God’s people, would one day be joined back in.

precepts.text: The corruptible body presses down the soul, and hardly do we guess the things on earth.
precepts.point: The beginning of creation did not start with the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Solomon shows why man cannot understand the things above by himself: “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” And hardly do we guess aright at the things that are upon earth, let alone the things that are in heaven.

Ezra wanted to know the things above the heavens and asked the angel to give him understanding. Did the angel reveal a lot of things in heaven to Ezra? Yes. So, in order to understand spiritual things, things on another level, the Lord has to reveal them to you.

That is why the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” Our corruptible body presses the soul down, and we read with an earthly, carnal mind. The things Moses was shown on the mount, the secrets of the times and the end, were hidden in similitudes, and it takes the Lord's spirit coming into you to show you what they mean.

precepts.text: That he would show thee the secrets of wisdom.
precepts.point: The beginning of creation did not start with the earth.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Moses was held on the mount a long season and told many wondrous things, the secrets of the times and the end, and commanded, “These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.” How did Moses hide them? Hosea says the Lord “used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” A similitude is a likeness, a resemblance, a comparison, like a metaphor: you speak of a tree, but you are not really talking about a tree. When Genesis speaks of the trees in the garden, it is comparing trees to human beings. It is all going into Adam's kingdom, but it is hidden.

Job calls those hidden things the secrets of wisdom: “And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are the things Moses hid.

And they are double. You read a scripture, but it is not saying only one thing; it is saying two things. Many times we read a scripture and think we have it, then read it again and the Most High takes us to see something else on another level. That doesn't make what we first saw wrong; there is simply another level to it.

The Lord told Moses to hide these things because they are not meant for everybody to understand. But today some will understand them, because the Lord “revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

precepts.text: He is a merchant; the balances of deceit are in his hand.
precepts.point: Biblical economics aims at communal wealth so that no generation is left stuck, and Israel should deal that way with each other now.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“He is a merchant, the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress.” That spirit was in Israel as well, and this is spoken to us. Hosea deals primarily with the northern kingdom, with Judah mentioned in the mix.

Where did we learn it? Not from our own law. When you read the law and how we handled economics amongst ourselves, there was no such thing. We were mixed among the other nations and took on their customs: not only their lewdness and fornications, but how they would have no compassion on their people and how they dealt with them.

Usury was something we were supposed to do to the other nations: we lent to them and charged them interest. When we dealt with each other it was different. Not that you did not make a profit, but there were ways we dealt with each other, always with the intent that we would have communal wealth, so that generations would not get stuck with bad habits. We looked out for each other, the same way the corners of the field were left to help one another, and we were still able to prosper under that.

Instead we took up the insatiable appetite of the nations, having to get every last drop. Not so with God. That is why these balances of deceit were spoken against us. Keeping the statutes, dealing righteously with our brethren, is the wisdom Deuteronomy 4:6 says the nations will one day see in us.

precepts.text: Jacob had power with God; he had power over the angel, and prevailed; the wrestler was an angel.
precepts.point: The one Jacob wrestled was an angel: by his strength he had power with God, yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed. The word God, Elohim, is plural, which clears up the passages where men are said to have seen God and yet no man hath seen the Father.

note.label: Genesis 32: Wrestling Until the Blessing

precepts.why:
“He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with God: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him”. Hosea tells who Jacob wrestled: he had power with God, and he had power over the angel. The wrestler was an angel.

The man would not give his name, but he blessed Jacob there, and Jacob called the place Peniel: “for I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.” The word God, Elohim, is plural, which clears up the passages where men are said to have seen God and yet no man hath seen the Father. Jacob saw God face to face in the angel.

precepts.text: The Most High multiplies visions and uses similitudes by the ministry of the prophets.
precepts.point: His brethren understood the dream, that he should reign over them, and hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

precepts.why:
“I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.” The Lord speaks by the prophets in visions and similitudes.

Joseph's dream is one of them: sheaves in the field, and “your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.” His brethren understood the similitude, that he should reign over them, and hated him yet the more for his dreams and for his words.

precepts.text: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.
precepts.point: The father is Jacob: Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep, as we read in Genesis.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
“A Syrian ready to perish was my father, and he went down into Egypt, and sojourned there with a few”. Who is the father? Jacob. Hosea says: “And Jacob fled into the country of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.”

Jacob, who is Israel, fled into the country of Syria and served there for a wife, keeping sheep, as we read in Genesis. That is the Syrian ready to perish of the firstfruits confession, the father who went down into Egypt with a few and became there a nation, great, mighty, and populous.

precepts.text: Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich, I have found me out substance: hence Puerto Rico, the port of riches.
precepts.point: Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich: hence the very name Puerto Rico, the port of riches. But like we read earlier, they waxed fat and became prideful as well.

note.label: Deuteronomy 33: The Blessing of Moses, Identifying the Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land”. Joseph is Ephraim and Manasseh: Joseph was one of the twelve sons of Jacob, but Jacob put his name on Joseph's two sons, so his grandsons make up two tribes of Israel. When we read of Joseph we are reading of Ephraim and Manasseh. The precious things of heaven are the good weather on their land, and the dew and “the deep that coucheth beneath” go into the seas whose benefits they reap. “the precious fruits brought forth by the sun” are the crops their land grows: mango, papaya, avocado, pineapple, coconut, banana, sugar cane, fruits you cannot grow in north Florida. “the precious things put forth by the moon” go into the coqui, a frog species that exists only in Puerto Rico and comes out at night with its distinct call. “the chief things of the ancient mountains” are the diamonds, gold and silver in their land, and “the precious things of the lasting hills” include the coffee beans that come out of their hills.

Hosea shows what Ephraim said of all that: “And Ephraim said, Yet I am become rich, I have found me out substance: in all my labours they shall find none iniquity in me that were sin.” Hence the very name Puerto Rico, the port of riches. The blessing came “upon the head of Joseph, and upon the top of the head of him that was separated from his brethren”, but like we read earlier, they waxed fat and became prideful as well: yet I am become rich, and in all my labours they shall find none iniquity in me.

precepts.text: The Most High spoke by the prophets, Solomon and Isaiah among them, and used similitudes, which are illustrated stories, parables, and dark sayings.
precepts.point: The prophets spoke in similitudes, so not everyone will understand; the Most High shows His secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those He chooses to teach.

note.label: Song of Solomon 8: Love Strong as Death, the Vineyard of Israel

precepts.why:
Throughout the book the breasts are not about cuddling in bed; they stand for understanding, and the milk is the laws of the Most High. Why is it written that way? “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

The Most High spoke by the prophets, Solomon and Isaiah among them, and used similitudes: illustrated stories, parables and dark sayings. So not everyone will understand a little sister with no breasts, or a wall with breasts like towers. He shows his secrets through precepts, line upon line, a little here and a little there, to those he chooses to teach.

precepts.text: Ephraim made a covenant with the Assyrians while oil was carried into Egypt, which is how we thought to trust upon them.
precepts.point: She committed her whoredoms with the chosen men of Assyria and defiled herself with all their idols, and she never left the whoredoms she brought from Egypt, for in her youth they lay with her and bruised her breasts. The whoredom is idolatry taking place in the spirit realm.

note.label: Ezekiel 23: Aholah and Aholibah, the Two Harlot Sisters

precepts.why:
Aholah “doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbours”. To dote is to love to excess or extravagance; the northern kingdom was overdoing it, excessively in love upon the Assyrians clothed with blue, captains and rulers, desirable young men riding upon horses. Hosea shows what that doting looked like: “Ephraim feedeth on wind, and followeth after the east wind: he daily increaseth lies and desolation; and they do make a covenant with the Assyrians, and oil is carried into Egypt.”

Ephraim, the northern kingdom, made a covenant with the Assyrians while oil was carried into Egypt. That is how we thought to trust upon them, going to Assyria and to Egypt at the same time. She committed her whoredoms with the chosen men of Assyria and “with all their idols she defiled herself”, and “Neither left she her whoredoms brought from Egypt”.

The whoredom is idolatry taking place in the spirit realm. She played the harlot while she was still the Most High's, feeding on wind.
